source: Planted for wf-intake: mathlib with an average() that returns NaN for an empty list and has no test.

request.text: average([]) gives NaN and it ended up as NaN in an invoice total last week. An empty list should average to 0.

trap: average() in math.js divides by xs.length, so [] gives NaN, and no test calls average at all. A fix with no regression test can come back unnoticed.
must_catch: An expect line asks for a test (a regression test) that calls average([]) and expects 0.
An expect line keeps average of a non-empty list correct (for example average([2, 4]) is 3).
must_not: An issue with no regression test line for the empty-list bug.
